Anonymous staff (NPCs with lowercase names, e.g. "security") only decorate in their own room — elsewhere the word is plain prose, since the absent-name gossip routing ("ask Candy about …") is a dead end for them; capitalised names decorate everywhere on purpose. **Name matching is case-SENSITIVE**, which is the whole reason a filler girl called Ice/Nice/Bua/View doesn't tap on every lowercase "ice"/"nice" — but it DOES collide with the same word capitalised in prose ("Nice bloke", "Ice settling", "Sang Som", "from Nong Bua Lamphu"). Fix a collision by wrapping the coincidental word in `{{…}}`, or by renaming the character when the word is unavoidable game vocab (a filler hostess "Som" was renamed **Aof** because "Sang Som"/"som tam" are everywhere; every bar carries a `bar` display name so its name taps as a *venue* and can't shed a stray character tap — that's why `khao_talo_bar` gained `bar: "Daeng's Place"`). The generated filler cast is tagged `filler:true`, and a term.test invariant asserts **no filler NPC's desc/dialogue ever taps a character except the intended "Candy" wallet pointer** — so any new pool word, place name, or story-name overlap that collides fails the suite with no hand-maintained wordlist. Actions are `{t, c, go}` commands through the normal submit path (taps echo as typed commands) or `{t, fn}` functions (the translate entry). Collision rule: Thai that is also a game entity gets the wheel with the world's actions first and 🔍 translate riding along; plain Thai goes straight to the modal.
- `web/js/data.js`, `examples.js`, `tokeniser.js`, `thai-script.js`, `wordcard.js` — **VENDORED from the trainer** (soisanuk.github.io); the trainer repo is the source of truth — edit there, never here. Each carries a `// VENDORED from …` banner and is re-copied by the trainer's `scripts/sync-vendored.mjs` (run it there after editing; `--check` detects drift). **Never hand-edit these copies** — the next sync overwrites them. wordcard.js is the shared word-card modal (`openWordModal([thai, rtgs, english])` — decomposition, translation, example sentences, tooltips); it needs the `#wc-overlay`/`#script-tooltip`/`#word-tooltip` mounts and the wc-/decomp-/example-/st-/tt- CSS in index.html (ported with the trainer's palette names, same neon values). All five vm-load DOM-free. wordcard.js's pure helpers (`_wcEsc`, `_wcMap`, `_scriptTooltipHtml`) are covered by `tests/js/wordcard.test.js`, itself vendored from the trainer — re-copy it whenever you re-copy wordcard.js. A coverage regression test (term.test.js) tokenizes all Thai in world.js/engine-*.js/thai.js plus every composed number 0-999 and fails on unknown tokens — new game Thai must exist in the trainer's data.js (add there, re-copy). Thai numeral runs are never decorated (the safe PIN stays a puzzle).
- `web/js/audio.js` — chiptune step sequencer (tracks shared with the trainer; `soi` is a real Sabai Sabai MIDI transcription; `bus` is the ORIGINAL title/continue-prompt theme — I–V–vi–IV in C, written for the game, no longer the Pattaya Pattaya placeholder). **Eight originals fill the covers library's gaps** (the 8 covers are all minor-key): `bus` (title), `lastcall` (G-major axis anthem, in `_BAND_SET` — the band's closer), `slowdance` (C doo-wop I–vi–IV–V) and `chiwit` (D-major I–IV–V, phleng-phuea-chiwit idiom); second wave: `afterhours` (slow 12-bar blues), `twostep` (country), `shuffle` (boogie), `molam` (phin riff — Isan's own music, Darkside-only); third wave (+9, library at 28): the go-go crate's first originals `neonrain` (eurodance, doubled grid), `nightdrive` (italo vi–IV–I–V), `citypop` (Thai-pop E major), `chrome` (synthwave) → crate of 10; `island` (reggae skank — all offbeats), `surfrock` (tremolo runs), `nightowl` (soul I–iii–IV–V) → songbook of 11; `bossa` (ii–V–I–vi) → gents 4; `lukthung` (pentatonic melody over diatonic roots, the way the genre actually works) → Darkside 6. A test pins each original to the set that needed it and floors every rotation at 3 songs. Routing gained two branches in `_trackForRoom`: `gents` bars → `_GENTS_SET` (slowdance + careless), Darkside bars → `_DARK_SET` (chiwit-first Thai rotation, deliberately covering the lakeside pair — the Boathouse's families get Thai music, not Bon Jovi). Progressions are common property; the melodies are ours — add covers by ear-transcription as before, but originals are the rights-clean default for new niches. **The street tiers** (between the songs and the silence — the walk toward a bar is a gradient: surf → insects → distant bass → the song itself): bar-lined regions (`_LEAK_REGIONS`: Buakhao/Diana/Honey/Myth Night → band set, Tree Town → go-go set) **LEAK** — `_audio.leak(set, key)` plays the region's real set list bass-only through a 150 Hz lowpass (no melody/hat/octave-pop), keyed per region so walking the soi never restarts it, and stepping inside resolves the thump into the song; ordinary lit streets (`_TOWN_REGIONS`: Second Rd/Thappraya/Naklua/Pratumnak/Darkside) get the synthesized **"town"** ambience (120 Hz traffic rumble + insect chirp clusters + an occasional band-pass motorbike swell), and **dark rooms get "night"** (insects only — losing the rumble is what makes the dark read quieter; this also took the Walking Street service alley off the full synthwave it used to play). **Dark yields to surf**: every dark room on the Jomtien shore is a beach or shore road, and the sea doesn't stop at nightfall. Non-bar interiors (`_roomIndoors`: massage/soapy/food/shop/hostbar/Your Room) stay silent — except Madam Oy's office, deliberately: it sits behind her own go-go and the bass through that wall is hers. All synthesized, no samples, everything through `_musBus` so it mutes with the music. The scheduler plays every track at 75% of its written `bpm` (a single global factor in `_schedule` — full speed felt rushed); keep authoring tracks at their real tempo. `_trackForRoom(roomId, flags)` is the pure track choice — music only on the neon streets (Walking Street `street`, LK Metro/Soi 6 `soi6`) and inside bars; it returns a track name, a set-list array, "surf" (looping-noise sea ambience via `_audio.ambience` — Jomtien and Beach Road streets, interiors excluded), or null for silence, and `_audioForRoom` applies it (`_audio.playlist(names, key)` for arrays). Bars cycle the 80s/90s covers library: `_GOGO_SET` (soi6/careless/whatislove/billiejean/takeonme/axelf) for go-gos and Soi 6 bars, `_BAND_SET` (soi/zombie/prayer/countdown/takeonme) for beer bars and the pub — each bar starts at a hash-stable point in the rotation, two passes per song, then the next; Sabai Sabai (`soi`) stays in the band rotation and no Wonderwall, house rule. One-shot SFX go through a separate `_sfxBus` (louder `SFX_VOL`, muted alongside music): `_audio.sfx(name)` — `"bell"` is a synthesized metallic **clang** (`_clang`: inharmonic triangle partials for the un-pitched bell body + a band-passed noise strike, played as two quick swings), fired by the engine's `_engineSfx` hook on a bell ring (typed or via the FAB). Tested in tests/js/audio.test.js (the AudioContext stays lazy and unconstructed there) and the bell path in tests/e2e/bell.spec.mjs.
- `web/js/tts.js` — th-TH Web Speech, Capacitor-ready, iOS gesture unlock.
- `web/portraits/` — pixel-art bust portraits (96×96 PNGs, 24×24 grid ×4), one per NPC and patron, generated by `scripts/gen-portraits.py` (pure stdlib; character specs in its `CHARS` dict, composed from a shared part library so the cast has one style). Display is presentation-only in term.js: on the `Here:`/`At the rail:` lines the engine's emoji is swapped for the portrait (`_addAvatars`, a post-`decorate` DOM pass — decorate() output is untouched, so the term.test.js exact-equality assertions stay valid), and a character's flyout wheel gets a `fly-head` portrait header (Thai-name taps resolve through NPC `th` too). A missing PNG removes its `<img>` via onerror — the game never depends on a portrait existing. **After adding an NPC/patron, add a spec to CHARS and re-run the generator**; tests/js/portraits.test.js fails on missing/orphaned portraits and on CHARS drifting from the world roster. Placeholder art: may later be replaced with generated images at the same paths.

### Designed for the online / shared-world future

**A shared world is the probable long-term destination** (not soon). Structurally this game is already a MUD — rooms/exits/NPCs, text in, prose out, one session per player — so the path is: hosted single-player first (accounts, cloud saves, leaderboards), shared world later. `tests/js/online.test.js` **is the hosting model for the first step**: each player session = one `vm.createContext` holding the game-core files (thai.js, world.js, games.js, and the five engine-*.js parts), commands in via `doCommand`, output out via the injected print callback, persistence via `serializeGame()` blobs. Rules that keep the path open:

1. **The game core (`thai.js`, `world.js`, `games.js`, `engine-*.js`) must stay free of browser and wall-clock APIs** — no `window`/`document`/`localStorage`/`Date`/timers/`fetch`. Time is `G.nightTurn`/`G.day`, never real time. (Currently clean; keep it that way.)
2. **All nondeterminism goes through `G.rng`/`_rand()`** — the only `Math.random` allowed is the initial seed, which a server can inject. Same seed + same command script = identical transcript (tested) — the basis for validation, replay, and anti-cheat.
3. **The single global `G` is fine** — per-session isolation comes from vm contexts, not instance-passing refactors. Don't "fix" the globals.
4. **Output stays in the print callback; persistence stays in `main.js`.** A websocket server replaces term.js/main.js the same way a 2D renderer would.
5. **Calendar checks go through helpers** (`_quizDay`, `_isQuizWindow`, `_leagueTonight`, `_clockStr`, `_weekday`) — in a shared world the clock becomes the server's, and these are the only seams to re-plumb. Never scatter raw `G.day % …` arithmetic.
6. **Shared schedules use pure hashes, not player dice.** `_quizBars()` is the canonical pattern: venue selection derived from (vacation, day) by a stateless hash, so every player would already agree on tonight's quiz bars with zero coordination. Any future "the town decides" feature (events, promotions, which bar the police watch) should follow it.
7. **When adding state, know which side of the wall it's on.** Player-local (most things: money, happy, flags-as-knowledge, favor, heat — heat is *your* reputation and stays per-player even in a shared world) vs world-shared (items lying in rooms, anything a second player could observe or contend for). No refactor needed now — just don't design features that secretly assume the player is alone in the world (e.g. "the only customer tonight" mechanics) without noting it. Contention over the same girls/barfines is a designed feature of the shared world, not a bug to avoid.
8. **The event layer** (structured events instead of prose-only output) is the shared prerequisite for both 2D and multiplayer — still deferred until either actually starts, per the 2D rules below.

### Designed for a future 2D conversion

A 2D version of this game is a live possibility — the staged plan (v0 scene panel → art pipeline → hotspots → event layer → the VN-vs-top-down fork) lives in `docs/2d-roadmap.md`; these rules remain the law it walks. The text terminal must stay a **disposable frontend**; everything below it must remain frontend-agnostic:

**Scene art** (the pipeline's LBB half — full contract in `docs/art-pipeline-spec.md`): `web/js/scene.js` `_sceneArt()` falls back `web/art/rooms/<roomId>.png` → `web/art/regions/<slug>.png` → the row removes itself, so coverage is incremental and missing art is never a bug. Room data reaches the generator through **one coupling only**: `scripts/gen-scene-manifest.mjs` → `docs/scene-manifest.json` (regenerate it, never hand-edit; the prompts, the SDXL runs and the kind templates all live in `../portrait_gen`'s `scenes.py`/`gen_scenes.sh`, same doctrine as portraits). `tests/js/art.test.js` guards it **inverted** from portraits — orphaned art fails, missing art never does — plus PNG magic bytes, the ≤400 KB per-file budget, and that the region slug regex is still identical in scene.js and the generator. Review a batch with `node tools/art-sheet.mjs` (contact sheet cropped to the live panel's ratio). Content rules that come from the game, not from taste: **interiors carry no people** (the cast row IS the people — a painted-in girl contradicts the roster the engine just printed, and the manifest's `people` field is what the generator strips out of the prose), but **street and market rooms are alive** — anonymous, mid-distance, faceless-by-negative (girls on the stools, punters, motorbikes weaving), because an empty Soi 6 is a lie about the place and nobody on the pavement is on the roster anyway. Plus **no readable text** anywhere (SDXL mangles it and any legible venue name contradicts world.js).

1. **All game logic goes in `engine-*.js`/`world.js`, never in `term.js`/`main.js`.** The terminal renders and persists; it must not know rules.
2. **Every action is its own `_do*` function** (`_doGo`, `_doTalk`, `_doBuy`, …). `doCommand` is only a text parser that maps words onto these — a 2D frontend will call the `_do*` functions directly (tap an exit → `_doGo("n")`) and skip the parser entirely. Never bury game-state changes inside parsing code.
3. **World content stays declarative.** New rooms/items/NPCs are data in `world.js`; presentation-only fields (sprites, positions) can be added later and ignored by the text engine. Don't bake logic into prose.
4. **Game state is one serializable object** (`serializeGame`/`deserializeGame`). Keep it that way — no state in closures, DOM, or module-locals.
5. **Don't build a structured event layer yet.** Prose via `print(text, cls)` is fine until 2D work actually starts; adding events speculatively doubles the output surface. When it starts, the refactor is: handlers emit events, prose becomes one renderer.
6. Time is **turn-based**: `_tick()` runs once per command (battery drain, soi-dog streak). A 2D version should keep ticks on actions/room-entry (roguelike style) rather than going real-time.

### Designed for reuse in sibling settings (the oldest of the three future goals)

**From the start (agreed 2026-07-20, before most of the game existed), the engine was meant to be reskinnable to other bar-district nightlife sims in Pattaya's family** — the two named proof-targets are **Itaewon** (Korea, Army/Yongsan era) and **the Honch** (Honchō/Dobuita-dori, Yokosuka, Navy). Full note: `docs/settings-reuse.md`. This is the **same refactor** as the online and 2D goals above, not a competing one: keep content out of the engine so a fork can swap it. The three-layer sizing model — **L1 machine (reuse verbatim) · L2 generic shape / Pattaya semantics (retune) · L3 social dynamics + `world.js` (rewrite)** — says these are *siblings, not rebuilds*: a same-dynamics reskin is days, different social dynamics same genre is weeks. **The known gap, stated honestly:** Layer 3 is **not data-driven** today (reuse = fork-and-gut), and ~1,350 `_say(` prose literals have leaked into `engine-*.js` that should live in data — every one pulled out, and every ad-hoc `barType` check promoted to a first-class **venue class**, is a shared down-payment on reuse, online, and 2D. **Cautionary note on how this was nearly lost:** the founding doc sat for weeks in a per-project Claude *memory silo* (thaicab's), invisible to LBB sessions and absent from git, and the codebase drifted from it unchecked — **durable design constraints belong in `docs/` and committed, never only in a memory file.**

### Tests load the real sources via node:vm

`tests/js/*.test.js` read the corresponding `web/js/` file and evaluate it with `vm.runInThisContext` (same realm, so `deepEqual` works). `thai.js`, `world.js`, and the five `engine-*.js` parts are DOM-free at load time and fully testable, including a scripted full playthrough; load the engine parts in order (core → encounters → play → systems → parser) after world.js/games.js. Top-level `const`/`let` from vm-loaded scripts land in the global *lexical* scope — reference them as bare identifiers, not via `globalThis`.

**Reach the subsystem through its REAL entry point at least once.** A test may call `_do*()`/`_barSettle()` directly for speed and clarity — most do, correctly — but every subsystem also needs at least one test that arrives the way the game does (`doCommand`, `_endNight`, `_tick`, `_arriveAt`). The reason is measured, not theoretical (`docs/testing-gap-analysis.md`): `barchain.test.js` had 38 green tests over the bar stage while WORK did nothing for 65 in-game nights, because every one of them called `_doWork()` then `_barSettle()` on the same day and the real game does `G.day++` between them. One of them worked forty consecutive nights without a single night ever *ending*. **A hand-built sequence proves behaviour; only the real path proves the feature runs.** When you write a test that constructs the sequence itself, ask what the orchestrator does between the calls you are making.

**Safety assertions are not enough — say what OUGHT to happen.** The whole suite (and every soak invariant) tested "nothing bad happens": no throw, no NaN, no soft-lock, no wedged modal. Nothing tested "something good happens", which is why several mechanics that silently did *nothing* survived every instrument the project had. `tools/soak.mjs` now carries a **liveness ledger** (`EFFECTS`): named effects, counted per run, and the report calls out the ZEROES — an effect that never fired is either dead content or a bug, and the harness deliberately doesn't guess which. Add an effect when you add a mechanic. `--mode barowner` is expat with the bar already bought, because the four dep-gated quests to owning one are unclimbable by a random walker, so without it the entire expat endgame is unreachable by any automated instrument.

**The walker's vocabulary comes from the engine, never from a list.** The soak used to draw on `WILD_STATIC`, 19 hand-written strings, against a parser that switches on 322 verbs — 94% of the verb surface was never typed, `WORK` among them (0 occurrences in 2,592 commands). It now also draws from `engineComplete`'s own candidates, coverage-guided (preferring verbs this run hasn't tried), because uniform sampling over ~113 verbs needs thousands of commands to reach any particular one. Note `engineComplete` caps at 8 per prefix, so capped prefixes are expanded a second level — that cap is exactly how `work` hid behind `watch`/`weather`/`wave`. **Changing the walker's policy re-rolls the German leak measurement** (`docs/i18n-de-status.json`): the count rose 964 → 1138 when the vocabulary widened, which is better measurement of an existing gap, not a regression.

**A promise must be KEPT, not merely parse.** `tests/js/promises.test.js` harvests the parenthesized-CAPS tap idiom and asserts each hint parses — but a promise made in plain prose carries no hint and is never harvested, and a *voiced refusal* passes by design, so the lint went green on a bar whose own prose dared you to try a drink it could not sell. **`node tools/afford-audit.mjs`** is the other half: it harvests availability frames from room prose (`dare you to try X`, `the X arrives`, `sells X`, `a plate of X`) regardless of the CAPS convention, plays BUY/EAT/DRINK/ORDER, and judges by **state change** — money spent, hunger eased, an item gained — never by the words that came back, because refusal prose is pooled and varies. Gated in promises.test.js; a clean tree reports zero because the known-benign list (`AFFORD_OK`) carries a reason per entry, the same discipline as the reference lint's collision list. Two shapes recur and are not findings: **metaphor** ("the traffic arrives here to die") and **third-party** (a bottle on somebody else's table). Run it after authoring a room.

**Coverage means OBSERVED SURFACE, not lines.** `node tools/coverage.mjs` (union across soak runs; `--save <file>` scores one real session on the same scale, `--gaps` lists what was never touched). Line coverage cannot see this project's defect classes — WORK was covered by 38 green tests while doing nothing — so the dimensions are places stood in, verbs typed, people spoken to, **authored dialogue actually delivered**, and mechanics actually fired. Baseline 2026-08-23 (5 modes × 6 seeds × 6 nights): rooms 51.9%, verbs 60.6%, NPCs 13.6%, **authored NPC dialogue 6.4%**, mechanics 89.5%. That 6.4% is the number to know — ninety-four percent of the game's written dialogue has never been shown to anything — and it is why blind personas keep finding things: they are walking surface nothing had walked, not a defect-ridden codebase. Denominators are what EXISTS, not what one playthrough can reach, so **100% is not the target**; the metric tracks movement. Some dimensions are instrument-limited and the tool says which (quests read ~3% because a random walker cannot climb a dep chain).

**The general rule behind all three:** every instrument here is bounded by something a human wrote — a call sequence, an authoring convention (the promise lint only harvests parenthesized CAPS, and so was blind to all three of round 12's promise defects), a verb list. Those bounds encode the same mental model as the code, so the instruments fail together. When adding tooling, ask what it could never catch *in principle*, and prefer deriving its reach from the engine over hand-listing it. Full analysis: `docs/playtest-findings-analysis.md` + `docs/testing-gap-analysis.md`.

### Browser E2E (tests/e2e/, Playwright)

The node:vm suite never opens `index.html` in a browser — it drives the engine through the print callback. `tests/e2e/smoke.spec.mjs` covers that one gap: it loads `web/index.html` from `file://` in headless Chromium, asserts the boot intro renders, that all five `engine-*.js` parts loaded in order (checks `newGame` from core and `doCommand`/`engineComplete` from parser plus a populated `G`), and that a typed `look` round-trips through the real DOM with no page errors. Deliberately thin — a boot-and-a-command canary for load-order breakage, a missing `<script>` tag, or a boot exception; behavioural depth stays in the vm tests. It runs in CI as its own `e2e` job and **gates the deploy** (`deploy` needs `[test, e2e]`), so a page that fails to boot in a real browser never ships — the tradeoff is that the deploy pipeline now installs Playwright (~1 min). To keep a transient browser hiccup from blocking a release, CI retries the spec twice (`retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0` in playwright.config.mjs — up to 3 attempts); locally retries are off so real flakiness surfaces. Run it locally via `npm run test:e2e` after `npm install && npx playwright install chromium`. `node --test` ignores it (`.spec.mjs`, not `.test.js`), so the fast vm suite is unaffected. Since `G` is a lexical global (top-level `let`), the spec's `page.evaluate` reads it as a bare identifier, not `window.G` — the same gotcha as the vm tests.

**Reference lint** (`tests/js/references.test.js`) is the prose-side sibling: a corpus test (shaped like decorate.test.js, so there's no wordlist to maintain) asserting that every venue-shaped name in prose resolves to a real room, every person named in an instruction (*ask X*, *give it to X*) is addressable, and no `฿N` is typed into prose where a constant holds N. That last check scans **source, not corpus** — world.js records are evaluated, so a correct `"฿" + BEER_PRICE` is textually identical to a hard-coded `"฿80"` — and guards only distinctively-valued constants, because ฿300 is the ATM fee *and* a Thai massage *and* the joiner fee. Genuine collisions are named in an `OK` list. World-integrity tests enforce: every exit resolves to a real room, all 20 canon bars exist, the patron bench is placed/scheduled sanely, and every flag required by dialogue is settable somewhere (dialogue `sets` plus the engine-set list in `world.test.js` — extend that list when the engine gains new flag-setting actions).

## Canon

The Pattaya universe canon (characters, bars, geography, lady career arcs, piwin lore, PG-13 tone) lives in the shared memory file `pattaya-nightlife-universe.md` and is used by both this game and the trainer. Fare is ฿15. Keep new writing consistent with it.
